key_insight: Machine-learning clocks derived from physiological waveforms predicted age, with accelerated waveform aging associated with higher odds of cardiovascular disease—not cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: Waveform-based aging clocks may offer investigational cardiovascular health biomarkers, but these findings do not establish clinical utility.
method: Extracted over 840 time-, frequency-, and statistical-domain features per cardiac cycle from PPG and arterial blood pressure waveforms.
Compared five machine-learning models to build PPGAge and ABPAge aging clocks.
Classified aging using predicted-minus-chronological age relative to model-specific error thresholds and tested associations with cardiovascular disease.
evidence_signal: Among 17,327 surgical patients, LightGBM achieved age-prediction correlations of 0.92 for both clocks; accelerated aging was associated with higher cardiovascular disease odds for PPGAge (OR 1.87, 95% CI 1.59–2.21) and ABPAge (OR 2.28, 95% CI 1.51–3.43).
watch_item: Findings from a perioperative cohort require external validation before generalization to other populations or routine clinical use.
paper_title: Physiological Waveform Features Based Aging Clocks Associate with Cardiovascular Disease
